    tsdst.distributions.weibull_regression_post¶

    tsdst.distributions.weibull_regression_post(parms, X, Y, status=None, l_scale=1, neg=False, log=True)[source]¶

    Evaluate the posterior for covariate-dependent Weibull shape and a shared scale.

    Parameters:
    parmsnumpy.ndarray

    Intercept and shape-regression coefficients, followed by log Weibull scale. The last value is a distribution-scale parameter; l_scale is the separate coefficient-prior scale argument.

    Xnumpy array (numeric)

    The independent variables (or feature matrix), where the first column is a dummy column of 1’s (for the intercept).

    Ynumpy.ndarray

    Positive event or right-censoring times, one per feature row.

    statusnumpy array (int, bool) or None

    Indicates status used for censoring, in this case, right censoring. An array of 1’s and 0’s, such that a 1 indicates an event, and 0 is the censored observation. If None, it will assume there are no censored events. Default is None.

    l_scalefloat, optional

    Positive Laplace coefficient-prior scale. The default is 1. A slope contributes abs(beta)/l_scale to the negative log posterior. The estimator sets this scale to 2*C. Matching an external L1 penalty also requires matching likelihood and intercept conventions.

    negbool, optional

    Return negative density. The default value is False.

    logbool, optional

    Return log-density. The default value is True.

    Returns:
    float

    The posterior density (height of the posterior density)

    Notes

    The coefficient vector is sampled on the real line. Shape is exp(X @ parms[:-1]), which enforces positivity. Weibull scale is exp(parms[-1]). The intercept has a normal prior with standard deviation 10, the slopes have Laplace priors with scale l_scale, and the positive Weibull scale has a Gamma prior with shape 0.01 and scale 100. The final parms[-1] contribution is the log-scale Jacobian for that Gamma prior. No extra shape-link Jacobian is required because the coefficient priors are defined on the sampled coefficients themselves.

    Events contribute a Weibull log density. Right-censored times contribute log survival. The event mask is applied to the matching observation shapes in both density terms.
